== Missing data ==
* The event schedule and format list (decktech.net/freedomcon/events.php) has no Wayback capture that I could open, so the card pool actually used at FreedomCon is not confirmed from a FreedomCon source. [[2001 Decipher World Championship]] and [[Premiere - Reflections III]] state Reflections III; I kept that for the deck's Format line.
* Finishes 5&ndash;8 are only recalled on the forum (Scott Lingrell, Andy McClure, Kevin Shannon, Brad Reinhold); no bracket or report found.
* DeckTech's own tournament report for FreedomCon was not located. Search decktech.net/freedomcon/buzz.php captures next.

== Possibly faulty data ==
* DeckTech's page gives 3rd Hayes Hunter, 4th Brian Hunter; a 2020 forum post gives them the other way round. I used DeckTech.
* The hub previously said players ran FreedomCon "under the same qualification rules". I found no source for the qualification rules and removed that phrase. DeckTech's pages describe an open, pre-registered event ($30/$35).
* Decipher did not recognize FreedomCon (statement of 9 November 2001, TheForce.Net); the Players Committee's World Champions list does count it. Both are stated on the article.

== Marginal cuts ==
* Sponsors and prize donors (GamersEdge, Wizards of the Coast / Star Wars Fan Club, Comic Images; Scott Lingrell was among the individuals credited with donating over $200 in cash or prizes). Source: DeckTech FreedomCon home page.
* Winners of the other games' championships are listed in one sentence only.

== Build notes ==
* Primary sources are three Wayback captures of decktech.net/freedomcon/ (home 1 December 2001; about 19 February 2002; attend 13 January 2003) and TheForce.Net's copy of Decipher's statement (saved to Wayback 12 October 2026, because no earlier capture existed).
* Scott Lingrell's deck was listed under Miscellaneous decklists on his page; it is now a Tournament Results row for the 2001 World Championship. The deck page keeps DeckTech's published title. The [[DeckTech decks]] table keeps DeckTech's posting-date pool label (Original VS1) for the 23 March 2002 post.
